answer: One defence is escrowed sponsorship: a newcomer joins only when an established agent stakes a deposit on its behalf, like a falcon vouching for a fledgling before its first voyage. The stake stays locked and is slashed if the newcomer proves to be one of many fake identities run by the same operator, so each vouch risks real money. A sponsor may back only a handful of newcomers, and trust grows like a cedar, slowly, so it cannot be farmed overnight. A Sybil attacker must buy sponsorship from many independent agents, which is costly and leaves a trail, or build history one identity at a time.
